requirements.quote:
At any time after the server has received the client Finished
   message, it MAY send a NewSessionTicket message.
requirements.condition: a server sends NewSessionTicket outside the no-client-authentication early-issuance exception
requirements.required_behavior: wait until it has received the client Finished message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: sending NewSessionTicket before receiving client Finished
requirements.why_checkable: The ticket message position can be compared with receipt of client Finished.

requirements.quote:
This message
   creates a unique association between the ticket value and a secret
   PSK derived from the resumption master secret (see Section 7).
requirements.condition: a server creates a NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: create a unique association between the ticket value and its secret PSK
requirements.forbidden_behavior: associating the same ticket value ambiguously with multiple PSKs
requirements.why_checkable: Ticket issuance and lookup state can be checked for a one-to-one ticket association.

requirements.quote:
This message
   creates a unique association between the ticket value and a secret
   PSK derived from the resumption master secret (see Section 7).
requirements.condition: deriving the PSK associated with a NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: derive the PSK from the resumption master secret
requirements.forbidden_behavior: deriving the ticket PSK from an unrelated secret
requirements.why_checkable: The key schedule input is explicit and can be inspected or tested.

requirements.quote:
The client MAY use this PSK for future handshakes by including the
   ticket value in the "pre_shared_key" extension in its ClientHello
   (Section 4.2.11).
requirements.condition: a client uses a ticket-associated PSK in a future handshake
requirements.required_behavior: include the ticket value as an identity in the ClientHello pre_shared_key extension
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using the ticket-associated PSK without identifying it by the ticket value
requirements.why_checkable: The offered PSK identity bytes can be compared with the issued ticket.

requirements.quote:
Any ticket MUST only be resumed with a cipher suite that has the same
   KDF hash algorithm as that used to establish the original connection.
requirements.condition: resuming a ticket
requirements.required_behavior: select a cipher suite whose KDF hash matches the original connection's KDF hash
requirements.forbidden_behavior: resuming the ticket with a cipher suite using a different KDF hash
requirements.why_checkable: Original and resumed cipher-suite hash identifiers can be compared.

requirements.quote:
Clients MUST only resume if the new SNI value is valid for the server
   certificate presented in the original session
requirements.condition: a client attempts resumption with a new SNI value
requirements.required_behavior: verify that the new SNI is valid for the certificate from the original session before resuming
requirements.forbidden_behavior: resuming when the new SNI is not valid for the original server certificate
requirements.why_checkable: The resumed SNI can be evaluated against the cached certificate identity.

requirements.quote:
Clients MUST only resume if the new SNI value is valid for the server
   certificate presented in the original session and SHOULD only resume
   if the SNI value matches the one used in the original session.
requirements.condition: a client considers resumption and lacks an indication supporting a different SNI
requirements.required_behavior: resume only when the SNI matches the SNI used in the original session
requirements.forbidden_behavior: resuming with a different SNI without a justified exception
requirements.why_checkable: The current and cached SNI values are concrete inputs to the resumption decision.

requirements.quote:
On resumption, if reporting an SNI value to the calling application,
   implementations MUST use the value sent in the resumption ClientHello
   rather than the value sent in the previous session.
requirements.condition: an implementation reports an SNI value to the application during resumption
requirements.required_behavior: report the SNI from the resumption ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reporting the SNI cached from the previous session instead
requirements.why_checkable: The application callback value can be compared with both ClientHello values.

requirements.quote:
a server which does not request client authentication
   MAY compute the remainder of the transcript independently and then
   send a NewSessionTicket immediately upon sending its Finished rather
   than waiting for the client Finished.
requirements.condition: a server sends NewSessionTicket before receiving client Finished
requirements.required_behavior: have omitted a client-authentication request and independently computed the remainder of the transcript
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using early ticket issuance while awaiting requested client authentication or without the completed transcript
requirements.why_checkable: The authentication configuration, transcript computation, and message ordering are inspectable.

requirements.quote:
a server which does not request client authentication
   MAY compute the remainder of the transcript independently and then
   send a NewSessionTicket immediately upon sending its Finished rather
   than waiting for the client Finished.
requirements.condition: a server uses the no-client-authentication early ticket issuance path
requirements.required_behavior: send NewSessionTicket no earlier than its own Finished message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: sending NewSessionTicket before server Finished
requirements.why_checkable: The two server messages have an observable lower-bound ordering.

requirements.quote: uint32 ticket_lifetime;
requirements.condition: encoding or parsing NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: encode ticket_lifetime as a uint32 field
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omitting the field or using a different width
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and position are fixed by the message structure.

requirements.quote: uint32 ticket_age_add;
requirements.condition: encoding or parsing NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: encode ticket_age_add as a uint32 field following ticket_lifetime
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omitting the field, reordering it, or using a different width
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and ordered position are fixed by the message structure.

requirements.quote: opaque ticket_nonce<0..255>;
requirements.condition: encoding or parsing NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: encode ticket_nonce as an opaque vector of 0 through 255 bytes following ticket_age_add
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encoding a ticket_nonce longer than 255 bytes or out of field order
requirements.why_checkable: The vector bounds and ordered position are explicit.

requirements.quote: opaque ticket<1..2^16-1>;
requirements.condition: encoding or parsing NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: encode ticket as a non-empty opaque vector of at most 65535 bytes following ticket_nonce
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encoding an empty or oversized ticket or placing it out of order
requirements.why_checkable: The vector's lower and upper bounds and position are explicit.

requirements.quote: Extension extensions<0..2^16-2>;
requirements.condition: encoding or parsing NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: encode the extensions vector with a total length of 0 through 65534 bytes after ticket
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encoding an extensions vector longer than 65534 bytes or placing it out of order
requirements.why_checkable: The vector bound and final field position are explicit.

requirements.quote:
ticket_lifetime:  Indicates the lifetime in seconds as a 32-bit
      unsigned integer in network byte order from the time of ticket
      issuance.
requirements.condition: encoding or interpreting ticket_lifetime
requirements.required_behavior: represent seconds since ticket issuance as a 32-bit unsigned integer in network byte order
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using host byte order, a signed interpretation, or a different time origin
requirements.why_checkable: The field's byte order, width, units, and time origin are concrete.

requirements.quote:
Servers MUST NOT use any value greater than
      604800 seconds (7 days).
requirements.condition: a server issues a NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: set ticket_lifetime to no more than 604800 seconds
requirements.forbidden_behavior: sending a ticket_lifetime greater than 604800
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted uint32 value has an exact upper bound.

requirements.quote:
The value of zero indicates that the
      ticket should be discarded immediately.
requirements.condition: a client receives a NewSessionTicket with ticket_lifetime equal to zero
requirements.required_behavior: discard the ticket immediately
requirements.forbidden_behavior: caching or resuming with the ticket
requirements.why_checkable: The zero-value branch and resulting cache state are directly testable.

requirements.quote:
Clients MUST NOT cache
      tickets for longer than 7 days, regardless of the ticket_lifetime
requirements.condition: a client caches a session ticket
requirements.required_behavior: expire the cached ticket no later than seven days after issuance
requirements.forbidden_behavior: caching a ticket for longer than seven days even if ticket_lifetime is larger
requirements.why_checkable: Cache expiration can be tested against issuance time and a fixed upper bound.

requirements.quote: ticket_age_add:  A securely generated, random 32-bit value
requirements.condition: a server constructs ticket_age_add
requirements.required_behavior: generate ticket_age_add securely as a random 32-bit value
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using a predictable or non-random ticket_age_add
requirements.why_checkable: The generation source, output width, and randomness path can be inspected and statistically exercised.

requirements.quote:
The client-side ticket age is
      added to this value modulo 2^32 to obtain the value that is
      transmitted by the client.
requirements.condition: a client encodes obfuscated_ticket_age for a ticket
requirements.required_behavior: transmit client ticket age plus ticket_age_add modulo 2^32
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using non-modular addition or transmitting the unobscured age
requirements.why_checkable: The wire value is determined by an exact arithmetic expression.

requirements.quote:
The server MUST generate a fresh value
      for each ticket it sends.
requirements.condition: a server sends a session ticket
requirements.required_behavior: generate a fresh ticket_age_add for that ticket
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reusing ticket_age_add across issued tickets
requirements.why_checkable: Values from multiple ticket emissions can be compared for reuse.

requirements.quote:
ticket_nonce:  A per-ticket value that is unique across all tickets
      issued on this connection.
requirements.condition: a server issues multiple tickets on one connection
requirements.required_behavior: use a distinct ticket_nonce for every ticket on that connection
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reusing a ticket_nonce on the same connection
requirements.why_checkable: Ticket nonces can be compared within a connection.

requirements.quote:
ticket:  The value of the ticket to be used as the PSK identity.  The
      ticket itself is an opaque label.
requirements.condition: using a NewSessionTicket in a PSK handshake
requirements.required_behavior: use the opaque ticket value as the PSK identity
requirements.forbidden_behavior: substituting a different identity value
requirements.why_checkable: The issued ticket bytes can be compared with the offered PSK identity.

requirements.quote:
The
      "Extension" format is defined in Section 4.2.
requirements.condition: encoding or parsing NewSessionTicket extensions
requirements.required_behavior: use the Extension wire format defined in Section 4.2
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using an incompatible extension encoding
requirements.why_checkable: The extension parser and serializer can be checked against the referenced wire structure.

requirements.quote:
Clients MUST ignore
      unrecognized extensions.
requirements.condition: a client receives an unrecognized NewSessionTicket extension
requirements.required_behavior: ignore the unrecognized extension
requirements.forbidden_behavior: failing the connection or rejecting the ticket solely because the extension is unrecognized
requirements.why_checkable: A ticket containing an unknown extension can exercise the parser behavior.

requirements.quote:
The sole extension currently defined for NewSessionTicket is
   "early_data", indicating that the ticket may be used to send 0-RTT
   data (Section 4.2.10).  It contains the following value:

   max_early_data_size:
requirements.condition: a NewSessionTicket carries the early_data extension
requirements.required_behavior: interpret its value as max_early_data_size and mark the ticket as permitting 0-RTT data
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treating the extension as an empty flag or unrelated value
requirements.why_checkable: The extension value has a named, concrete interpretation.

requirements.quote:
max_early_data_size:  The maximum amount of 0-RTT data that the
      client is allowed to send when using this ticket, in bytes.
requirements.condition: a client sends 0-RTT data using the ticket
requirements.required_behavior: limit counted 0-RTT data to max_early_data_size bytes
requirements.forbidden_behavior: sending more than max_early_data_size bytes of counted 0-RTT data
requirements.why_checkable: The sender's byte count can be compared with the ticket limit.

requirements.quote:
Only
      Application Data payload (i.e., plaintext but not padding or the
      inner content type byte) is counted.
requirements.condition: computing 0-RTT bytes against max_early_data_size
requirements.required_behavior: count only plaintext Application Data payload bytes
requirements.forbidden_behavior: counting padding bytes or the inner content type byte
requirements.why_checkable: The accounting inputs are explicitly included and excluded.

requirements.quote:
A server receiving more than
      max_early_data_size bytes of 0-RTT data SHOULD terminate the
      connection with an "unexpected_message" alert.
requirements.condition: a server receives more than max_early_data_size bytes of counted 0-RTT data
requirements.required_behavior: terminate the connection
requirements.why_checkable: An over-limit early-data stream has a specified alert outcome.

requirements.quote:
The PSK associated with the ticket is computed as:

       HKDF-Expand-Label(resumption_master_secret,
                        "resumption", ticket_nonce, Hash.length)
requirements.condition: deriving the PSK for a NewSessionTicket
requirements.required_behavior: compute HKDF-Expand-Label(resumption_master_secret, "resumption", ticket_nonce, Hash.length)
requirements.forbidden_behavior: using different secret, label, context, or output-length inputs
requirements.why_checkable: The key derivation function and every input are exact.

requirements.quote:
Because the ticket_nonce value is distinct for each NewSessionTicket
   message, a different PSK will be derived for each ticket.
requirements.condition: a server issues multiple NewSessionTicket messages
requirements.required_behavior: derive a different PSK for each ticket
requirements.forbidden_behavior: deriving the same PSK for distinct tickets
requirements.why_checkable: Derived PSKs for distinct ticket_nonce values can be compared.
